appTag: Kings · Two Kingdoms in the Steps of the Prophets
docTitle: The Way — Kings | Two Kingdoms in the Steps of the Prophets
metaDesc: From Solomon's temple, past the fire on Mount Carmel and Elisha's horses and chariots of fire, to the rivers of Babylon. Walk 41 scenes of the two kingdoms on a Bible map in the steps of the prophets, and hear the psalms of those places as songs.
mapAria: The way of Kings on a map of Judah, Israel, Aram and Babylon
introTag: Two kingdoms in the steps of the prophets, from Solomon's temple to the rivers of Babylon
introLead: Walk the map with Elijah, Elisha and Isaiah, and meet the kings of a kingdom torn in two.
introF1: Follow the places, from Jerusalem and Samaria, past Mount Carmel and Mount Horeb, all the way to Babylon
introF3: Hear the story read aloud, and listen to the psalms linked to each place as songs
landStep2: Read the story and the texts on the card, and press ▶ to hear it read aloud
landStep4: Gather the words of God and of the prophets in the '{words}' tab, and revisit the scenes you have walked with '{quiz}'
hisWords: Words of God and the Prophets
wordsHead: Words of God and the Prophets
wordsIntro: The words God spoke and the words the prophets proclaimed along the way of the two kingdoms, gathered in the order of the journey. Every saying is a fresh rendering of the original meaning in today's language.
odoTitle: Distance walked up to this scene (estimated road distance between places; steps at a 75 cm stride)
endLead: From Solomon's temple to the rivers of Babylon — thank you for walking with us.
blessing:
God is our refuge and strength, a great help always found in times of trouble. (Ps 46:1)
May the one who was there in the fire and in the still small voice speak on your way too, and build you up again where things have fallen down.
psalmHead: The song sung in this place
psalmNote: A song from the Psalms journey, sung in Korean. The music and lyrics were made with AI and refined by people.
lessons:
A king's heart decides a kingdom|When Solomon's heart turned to other gods, the kingdom split in two. The road of the kings who followed idols ended in ruin. (1 Kgs 11:9–11)
The God who keeps calling|God sent Elijah and Elisha and many prophets, calling again and again: turn from your evil ways. (2 Kgs 17:13)
A lamp that does not go out|Even when the kingdom fell and the people were carried into exile, God kept his promise that David would always have a lamp. (1 Kgs 11:36)
gospelBridge: One after another the kings fell, and the kingdom seemed to end by the rivers of Babylon. But from the line of Jehoiachin, released from prison, came the King who will never fall: Jesus (Matt 1:12–16). He proclaimed: the time has come, and the kingdom of God has come near. (Mark 1:15)
invite:
If the story of God you met on this road has stayed with you, come and meet Jesus, who stands at the center of that story. Walk 'The Footsteps of Jesus' from the beginning, and visit a church near you. May you meet God in worship and in his word, be adopted as his child, and know the joy of calling God 'Father.' (Rom 8:15)
He is still standing at the door, waiting for you. (Rev 3:20)
seekerHead: For those who don’t yet know him
